m117_p0_closure_decision.reason: M119 directly closes the identity-only and tail-bypass mechanism in a standalone behavioral fixed-latency kernel, but the actual M117 service stream and shared memory system are not connected.

m118_p0_closure_decision.directed_counterexample: An exact already-accepted event held through output backpressure was accepted a second time on simultaneous old-update retirement and generated a second update without protocol_error.
m118_p0_closure_decision.ready_valid_qualification: The retry is an upstream contract violation under strict ready/valid. It still demonstrates that M119 cannot itself provide the sequence-aware duplicate/replay proof demanded by M118 P0.

timeline: load1 consumes response0 and issues beat1
load2 consumes response1 and issues beat2
first event consumes response2 through complete_payload tail bypass

findings.finding: M119 has no sequence identity or accepted-event deduplication. An exact event held after acceptance through output backpressure was accepted again when the older update retired, producing two updates with no protocol_error.
findings.impact: M119 closes normal standalone event-to-update conservation but cannot close M118's heldout retry/replay exact-once premise. A duplicated contribution can invalidate the signed19 bound.
findings.required_action: Integrate sequence-tagged M117 service with M119 and M118, then prove planned, accepted and accumulated transactions are one-to-one under retry and recovery.

findings.finding: M119 is not instantiated behind M117; its independent load/event source directly supplies the expected three-beat grammar.
findings.required_action: Connect the exact M117 service interface and run cross-module cycle conservation under both service and update backpressure.

findings.finding: weight_rd_data is supplied by a behavioral model with exactly one cycle latency and no response-valid, retry, ECC or error signal.
findings.required_action: Bind a legal foundry SRAM/arbiter contract and prove the same tail timeline with its real latency and response semantics.

findings.finding: Every accepted load immediately owns a dedicated 256-bit read. Shared PWP/correction contention, arbitration delay and bank conflicts are not represented.
findings.required_action: Insert the shared arbiter and measure whether all three reads remain aligned without an extra tail cycle.

findings.finding: The memory request exposes only a 7-bit source/block key; M117 context is absent. Any operator/checkpoint/context bank selection is an unstated external invariant.
findings.required_action: Freeze external weight residency per context or extend/tag the weight request and verify context switches.

findings.finding: The 1824-bit signed19 update stops at a skid output and is not connected to M118 address, hazard, overflow or commit semantics.
findings.required_action: Miter each accepted M119 update into M118 and compare committed rows with an integer oracle.

findings.finding: No exact heldout descriptor/payload replay, macro-inclusive STA/PTPX or matched physical baseline exists; the M109 ratio remains projection only.
findings.required_action: Run exact trace integration first, then foundry macro timing/power against a matched baseline.

findings.finding: Load token legality checks beat/key/type but does not require row=0, negate=0 or last_for_key=0.
findings.suggested_action: Assert the complete M117 load token shape at the integration boundary.

findings.finding: Any 9-bit event row is accepted; the W384 range 0..383 is not checked locally.
findings.suggested_action: Assert row<384 or document that M117 is the sole trusted range checker.

findings.finding: update identity contains block and row only. Source is implicit in numeric data and sequence is absent, limiting downstream attribution and replay audit.
findings.suggested_action: Carry a verification-only or production sequence/source tag through the integrated miter.

findings.finding: The reverse/permuted/random and attack vectors are directed commercial simulation, not exhaustive equivalence or protocol proof.
findings.suggested_action: Add commercial formal proof for three-beat ordering, tail selection and elastic exact conservation.

findings.finding: Production sealed VCS attacks only a wrong first beat. Independent VCS adds retry, skip, key, type, duplicate and older-update fault-drain cases.
findings.suggested_action: Promote the independent negative matrix into the production regression without changing the frozen r1 receipt.
